name: stats-bold

frames.best_why: The counters are settled at 142 regions and the full image shows with no cursor over it.

tagline: A huge 10B+ tally counts up beside a hot pink photo and three small stats.
summary: A full-width stats section pairing an oversized 10B+ API-calls figure and a bright gradient image with three smaller metrics below: latency, regions and support hours. Numbers count up as it scrolls into view.
appearance: On black, a very large pale 10B+ sits at the left, followed by a small bold title and a two-line grey caption, with a wide pink-to-white gradient photo at right. A thin rule divides it from a row of three numbers, each with a tiny uppercase label.
behaviour: When the section enters view, 10B+, 0.1ms and 142 tick up from zero over about a second, and the lower row slides up and fades in. The 24/7 figure is static text. Nothing reacts to the pointer.
demo_content: The copy API Calls Monthly, a paragraph about zero latency, and a pink gradient photo from Unsplash.
use_when: A marketing page needs a compact proof section of large numbers, one hero metric and three supporting ones.
avoid_when: All copy and the photo are hardcoded, and the section insists on min-h-screen, so it cannot sit in a short page.
customise: Takes no props. The figures, copy, labels, image URL and full-screen-height layout all live in the file, so any change is a source edit.
weight_why: A few spans count up once on view; no continuous loop or canvas.

a11y.note: The photo's alt text is the vague phrase 'supportive img', and the count-up has no reduced-motion guard.

issues: The image alt text is the vague phrase "supportive img".
min-h-screen leaves large empty space on tall screens.
polish_why: Big type and bold colour work well; the full-screen height wastes space.
